articles.title: Jordanian security officer killed in stabbing attack in Amman
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: One Jordanian police officer was killed and another was injured in a stabbing attack outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Jordan’s capital, Amman, on Thursday, November 5. According to a statement issued by Jordan’s Public Security Directorate (PSD), the slain officer was identified as Corporal Jawad al-Salaytah. PSD also confirmed that the perpetrator was arrested by a police patrol that rushed into the site of the attack. Jordanian Government Communication Minister and Official Government Spokesperson Mohammad Momani said that the preliminary investigation revealed that the assault was a “cowardly terrorist attack.” Momani affirmed that “attacking security personnel while performing their duty is an assault on the prestige of the state and the rule of law, and an assault on every Jordanian.

articles.title: South Korea moves to join Iran War under US pressure
articles.author: Ju-Hyun Park
articles.content_excerpt: South Korea’s government has begun procedures to potentially join the US-Israeli war of aggression against Iran. On November 5, a vice-ministerial meeting affirmed a decision to expand the military capacities and operational area of the Cheonghae Unit, a blue-water naval force that has operated in the Gulf of Aden near the Red Sea as part of an “anti-piracy” mission since 2020. The revised mandate of the Cheonghae Unit would double its deployment area up to the waters of the Arabian Sea south of Duqm, Oman. This would place Republic of Korea (ROK) naval units on the fringes of the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz – areas Iran has declared closed to foreign military vessels. articles.title: Vegetation is claiming El Fasher, one year after it was depopulated by the RSF
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: One year after the UAE-backed Rapid Support Forces (RSF) massacred tens of thousands of civilians in El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur state in war-torn Sudan, the city remains largely depopulated. Vegetation is claiming what used to be busy markets and roads. Hospitals are bombed out and empty, and the mass graves are quiet. This is the picture painted by the satellite imagery analysis by the Yale School of Public Health Humanitarian Research Lab (HRL) in a report titled “El-Fasher, One Year Later .”​ Human activity is largely limited to just five of the city’s 24,307 square kilometers, in the Daraja Oula neighborhood, where RSF troops are based. articles.title: 40 years later, calls grow demanding the truth about Samora Machel’s death
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Forty years after the death of Samora Machel, Mozambique’s first president and leader of the country’s liberation movement (FRELIMO), the circumstances surrounding the plane crash that claimed his life remain contested. The tragedy, which occurred on October 19, 1986, in Mbuzini, in what was then South Africa’s eastern Transvaal, continues to raise questions about whether the crash was an accident or an act of sabotage involving the apartheid government. At the 40th anniversary ceremony on October 19, 2026, Mozambican President Daniel Chapo said the investigations of the past four decades had not dispelled the doubts. articles.title: The Country Says “No” to Trump: Not Just Congress, the Blue Tsunami Flips Statehouses Across U.S.
articles.content_excerpt: We examine the results of Tuesday’s historic U.S. midterm elections with Daniel Nichanian, editor-in-chief of Bolts . In addition to taking back the House and Senate, Democrats also made major gains at the state level and will control a majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years. Democrats also flipped 12 state legislative chambers. “The size of the wins for Democrats in statewide races was wild,” says Nichanian. He identifies protecting abortion access, bolstering unions and ending police cooperation with ICE as some of the priorities Democrats are likely to pursue.

articles.title: First Gen Z Congresswoman: DSA’s Melat Kiros on Corruption, Medicare for All & Israel
articles.content_excerpt: The Democratic Socialists of America made major gains in this year’s U.S. midterms, electing not just the largest-ever socialist bloc to Congress, but also winning dozens of races at the state, county and municipal levels. Democracy Now! spoke with Congressmember-elect Melat Kiros on election night following her victory in Denver, Colorado. She identified Medicare for All as her top priority and said progressives must lay the groundwork “so that in ’29, when we have the House, the Senate and the White House, we can sign it into law on day one.” Kiros is a 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant and lawyer. In 2023, Kiros wrote an open letter about the danger of conflating antisemitism and criticism of Israel, for which she was fired by her law firm. She won a major upset in the Democratic primary

articles.title: France’s student strikes
articles.author: Danielle Bullock
articles.content_excerpt: F rench students have been protesting in the largest numbers since the historic May 1968 Paris uprising. Protests began last month in Paris’s northern suburbs, where students have struggled to learn in crumbling, pest-infested schools with too few teachers. Students say the government’s latest budget isn’t enough to fix the school system’s failings, and they are demanding more. Public anger over the budget and abysmal school conditions has spread—and so have the protests; students have been blocking high schools and protesting in the streets in the thousands. The government’s response has been heavy-handed and violent; there have been many recorded incidents of police brutality against young and vulnerable high school students.
